title: Sample enrichment for single-nucleus sequencing using concanavalin A-conjugated magnetic beads
protocol: Perform cervical dislocation on deeply anesthetized mice using 5% isoflurane.
Quickly dissect the hypothalamus and place it under a fluorescence stereomicroscope.
Isolate the tissue containing GFP+ Pomc-Cre neurons from individual Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice and transfer it onto dry ice.
Collect the tissue from a similar region in wild-type mice without GFP fluorescence and transfer it onto dry ice.
Store brain tissues in a -80°C freezer.
Prepare 50 mL of Sucrose Cushion buffer in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add 8 mL of Sucrose Cushion buffer to individual 50 mL Nalgene centrifuge tubes.
Keep the tubes on ice throughout the experiment.
Prepare 50 mL of Homogenization buffer in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Keep the tube on ice throughout the experiment.
Add 1 mL of Homogenization buffer into individual 2 mL Dounce tissue grinder tubes.
Place dissected brain tissues from Pomc-Cre;CAG-SfGFP mice into individual grinder tubes.
Dounce the brain tissues in individual grinder tubes 20 times using a Dounce grinder pestle.
Place a 30 μm pre-separation filter over a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Soak the filter with 0.5 mL of Homogenization buffer.
Extract approximately 1 mL of tissue homogenate from each grinder tube and filter it through the 30 μm filter into the 15 mL Falcon tube.
Rinse individual grinder tubes with 1.25 mL of Homogenization buffer.
Collect the liquid with a pipette and filter it through the 30 μm filter into the 15 mL Falcon tube.
Repeat rinsing once.
Gently transfer the filtered homogenate (∼4 mL) from the 15 mL Falcon tube into individual Nalgene centrifuge tubes containing the Sucrose Cushion buffer.
Balance the tubes and centrifuge them at 47,000 g for 1 h at 4°C.
Use a pipette to carefully discard the top and middle layers of the liquid after centrifugation.
Prepare 50 mL of Wash buffer in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Resuspend the nuclei with 100 μL of Wash buffer and transfer them into a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Incubate the nuclei isolated from Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice with several antibodies.
Employ an anti-NeuN-Alexa Fluor 647 antibody to selectively label Pomc-Cre+ nuclei from neurons.
Use a dual color sorting approach utilizing both Fluor 647 and GFP.
Incorporate a multiplexing strategy by utilizing barcoded antibodies against nuclear pore complex (NPC) proteins.
Utilize barcoded anti-GFP antibody to specifically label GFP+ Pomc-Cre nuclei.
Add 1 μL of anti-NeuN-Alexa Fluor 647 antibody to the nuclei isolated from Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice.
Add 0.5 μL of each barcoded anti-NPC antibody to the nuclei isolated from Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice.
Add 1 μL of barcoded TotalSeq anti-GFP antibody to the nuclei isolated from Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice.
Add 1 μL of anti-NeuN-Alexa Fluor 647 antibody to the nuclei isolated from one wild-type mouse for single-color control.
Mix the nuclei and antibodies well.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 10 min.
Wash the nuclei by adding 3 mL Wash buffer.
Centrifuge the mixture using a swinging bucket centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully remove the liquid using a pipette.
Repeat the washing step two more times.
Resuspend nuclei with 100 μL of Wash buffer.
Pool all antibody-treated nuclei from Pomc-Cre;CAG-Sun1/sfGFP mice.
Filter them through a 30 μm filter into a BD sorting tube.
Similarly, filter the nuclei designated for sorting controls and place them into separate sorting tubes.
Sort the dual-color nuclei (Alexa Fluor 647 and GFP) into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 100 μL of Wash buffer.
Thoroughly mix the ConA-beads solution.
Add 11 μL of ConA-beads to a new 0.2 mL PCR tube and place it on ice.
Activate the ConA-beads by adding 100 μL of ConA-beads Activation buffer.
Mix the solution using a pipette.
Incubate the solution on ice for 15 min.
Place the PCR tube on a magnet rack (in front of a magnet).
Wait for 1–2 min until the slurry clears and then remove the liquid using a pipette.
Repeat steps 26-28 one more time.
Resuspend the activated beads with 11 μL of Wash buffer and place the tube on ice.
Extract 10 μL of the activated beads and add them into the Eppendorf tube with the sorted nuclei.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Place the tube on a magnet rack (in front of a magnet) for 1–2 min until the slurry clears and then remove the liquid with a pipette.
Resuspend the nuclei/beads with 6 μL of Wash buffer.
Gently mix well on ice.
Use 1 μL of the nuclei/beads mixture to determine the concentration of the nuclei.
Add DAPI or use GFP signals for counting nuclei.
Adjust the concentration to 1,000–5,000 nuclei/μL.
Proceed with the 10× Single-nucleus Multiome pipeline using 5 μL of purified nuclei.
